text: CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) from autoimmune patients, including type 1 diabetes, poorly control autologous proinflammatory responses versus controls; whether this dysfunction is causal or secondary is unclear. IL2RA polymorphisms increase autoimmune risk, but their link to Treg function was unexamined. Using healthy subjects to avoid disease confounders, researchers found a type 1 diabetes-associated IL2RA haplotype correlates with diminished IL-2 responsiveness in antigen-experienced CD4+ T cells, measured by STAT5a phosphorylation. It also associates with lower FOXP3 expression by Tregs and reduced suppression of autologous effector T cell proliferation. These data suggest molecular and cellular mechanisms by which IL-2RA polymorphisms affect immune regulation and autoimmune/inflammatory disease susceptibility.
